name: Slippery Nipple
description: Sambuca under Irish cream, layered so the two stay separate until you drink them. Named with the subtlety of its era.
funFact: The layers hold because Irish cream is less dense than sambuca; add the grenadine last and it sinks through both to sit at the bottom as a red dot.

steps: Pour the sambuca into a shot glass.
Float the Irish cream over the back of a barspoon so it sits cleanly on top.
Drop two drops of grenadine through the centre — they should sink.
Serve immediately, before the layers bleed.

name: Duck Fart
description: Kahlúa, Irish cream and whisky in three layers. Alaska's contribution to the shooter canon, and the name is not explained.
funFact: It was invented at the Peanut Farm bar in Anchorage in the 1980s, and Alaskans defend both the drink and its name with more energy than either strictly warrants.

steps: Pour the Kahlúa into the bottom of a shot glass.
Float the Irish cream over a barspoon to make the middle layer.
Float the whisky on top the same way.
Serve immediately and drink in one.

name: Alabama Slammer
description: Southern Comfort, amaretto and sloe gin with orange juice — a shot in some bars, a tall drink in others, sweet in both.
funFact: It spread through American college bars in the 1970s and is usually associated with the University of Alabama, though no one has ever produced evidence for that.

steps: Shake all ingredients briefly with ice.
Strain into a shot glass, or into a tall glass over ice for the long version.
Add a squeeze of lemon if serving long.
Serve cold.

name: Red Headed Slut
description: Jägermeister, peach schnapps and cranberry — herbal and fruity at once, and far more drinkable than its reputation.
funFact: Jägermeister contains 56 botanicals and was formulated in 1934 as a digestif for hunters; its American career as a party shot would have baffled its inventor.

steps: Shake all ingredients with ice for 8 seconds.
Strain into a shot glass or a small rocks glass.
Serve cold, immediately.
For a longer version, pour over ice and top with more cranberry.

name: Woo Woo
description: Vodka, peach schnapps and cranberry. A Sex on the Beach with the orange juice removed, and better for it.
funFact: It belongs to a whole 1980s family built on peach schnapps, which the American market had barely heard of before 1985 and then could not get enough of.

steps: Shake all ingredients with ice for 8 seconds.
Strain into a shot glass, or over ice in a highball for a long version.
Garnish with a lime wedge if serving long.
Serve cold.

name: Purple Hooter
description: Vodka, raspberry liqueur and lime — bright purple, sharp and gone in one.
funFact: Chambord is made in the Loire from black raspberries and honey to a recipe claiming descent from a seventeenth-century royal liqueur — a grand pedigree for a bar shot.

steps: Shake all ingredients hard with ice for 8 seconds.
Double-strain into a chilled shot glass.
Serve immediately.
A lime wedge on the side is optional.

name: Surfer on Acid
description: Jägermeister, coconut rum and pineapple. Sounds alarming and tastes, unexpectedly, like a tropical dessert.
funFact: The coconut and pineapple mask Jägermeister's bitterness almost completely, which is why people who insist they hate Jäger reliably finish this one.

steps: Shake all ingredients with ice for 8 seconds.
Strain into a shot glass or small rocks glass.
Serve cold.
Scale it up over ice for a longer drink.

name: Scooby Snack
description: Melon liqueur, coconut rum, pineapple and cream, shaken to a pale green froth. A dessert disguised as a shot.
funFact: Midori was launched in the US in 1978 at Studio 54, and the whole family of green shots that followed exists because of that one marketing party.

steps: Shake all ingredients hard with ice for 10 seconds.
Double-strain into a shot glass.
It should be pale green and foamy on top.
Serve immediately.

name: Liquid Marijuana
description: Blue curaçao and melon liqueur with coconut rum and pineapple, turning an improbable green. Named for the colour, nothing else.
funFact: Blue curaçao plus yellow pineapple juice makes green — the same colour trick behind half the novelty drinks invented between 1975 and 1995.

steps: Shake all ingredients with ice for 8 seconds.
Strain into a shot glass or over ice in a rocks glass.
The colour should be a clear green.
Serve immediately.

name: Three Wise Men
description: Jack Daniel's, Jim Beam and Johnnie Walker in equal measure, neat. No mixer, no ceremony, no mercy.
funFact: Variations swap in Jose Cuervo to make the Four Horsemen, or add Jägermeister for the Five Wise Men — the joke scales in exactly one direction.

steps: Pour all three whiskies into a shot glass.
Do not stir, chill or dilute — the point is that it is undignified.
Serve at room temperature.
Drink in one.

name: Prairie Fire
description: Tequila and Tabasco. Two ingredients, one of which is hot sauce, and no attempt at balance.
funFact: It belongs to the dare category of shots rather than the drinking category, and the capsaicin genuinely does mask the tequila — which is the only reason it works at all.

steps: Pour the tequila into a shot glass.
Add the Tabasco directly on top.
Do not stir.
Drink in one, and have something cold ready.

name: Cement Mixer
description: Irish cream held in the mouth, then lime juice added. It curdles on your tongue. That is the entire drink.
funFact: The curdling is real chemistry: lime juice drops the pH below the point where casein proteins stay suspended, and they clump instantly — the same reaction that makes cheese.

steps: Pour the Irish cream into a shot glass and the lime juice into a second.
Take the Irish cream into your mouth but do not swallow.
Add the lime juice and hold both for a few seconds.
Swallow, and accept the consequences.

name: Chartreuse Bomb
description: A shot of green Chartreuse dropped into a glass of cider or beer. Bartender currency, and traded as such.
funFact: Green Chartreuse is still made by Carthusian monks to a recipe held by two of them at a time; supply shortages since 2021 have made bartenders noticeably less willing to bomb it.

steps: Pour the cider into a small glass, leaving room.
Fill a shot glass with green Chartreuse.
Drop the shot glass into the cider.
Drink immediately, before it dilutes.

name: Lemon Drop Martini
description: The Lemon Drop scaled up into a coupe with a sugared rim — sharper and more grown-up than the shot it came from.
funFact: Norman Jay Hobday created the original at Henry Africa's in San Francisco in the 1970s, a bar widely credited with inventing the fern-bar format.

steps: Rim a chilled coupe with lemon and caster sugar.
Shake the vodka, triple sec, lemon juice and syrup hard with ice.
Double-strain into the rimmed coupe.
Garnish with a lemon twist.
recipe.garnish: Lemon twist on a sugared rim

name: Blue Kamikaze
description: A Kamikaze with blue curaçao standing in for the triple sec. Same drink, different colour, considerably more popular.
funFact: Blue curaçao and triple sec are the same liqueur with food colouring added, which means the Blue Kamikaze is chemically a Kamikaze that photographs better.

steps: Shake all ingredients hard with ice for 8 seconds.
Double-strain into a chilled shot glass.
Serve immediately.
Scale up into a coupe for a full-size version.

name: Tokyo Tea
description: A Long Island Iced Tea with melon liqueur in place of the cola. Green, enormous and exactly as strong as its parent.
funFact: The Long Island family is defined by five white spirits plus a modifier: cola makes the original, cranberry the Long Beach, blue curaçao the Blue Motorcycle, and melon this one.

steps: Fill a tall glass with ice.
Add all the spirits, the melon liqueur and the lemon juice.
Top with lemon-lime soda.
Stir once from the bottom.
Garnish with a lemon wheel and a cherry.

name: Long Beach Iced Tea
description: The Long Island with cranberry instead of cola. Pink rather than brown, and it fools people just as effectively.
funFact: The whole Long Island format exists to look like iced tea, which is why the original uses cola — the cranberry version abandons the disguise entirely and keeps the strength.

steps: Fill a tall glass with ice.
Add the five spirits and the lemon juice.
Top with cranberry juice.
Stir once from the bottom up.
Garnish with a lemon wedge.

name: Adios Motherfucker
description: The Long Island turned blue: five spirits, blue curaçao and lemonade. Also sold politely as an AMF.
funFact: Most bars list it as 'AMF' on the menu to avoid printing the full name, which has done nothing at all to stop customers ordering it by the full name.

steps: Fill a tall glass with ice.
Add the four spirits, blue curaçao and sour mix.
Top with lemon-lime soda.
Stir once to bring the colour through.
Garnish with a lemon wheel.

name: Irish Car Bomb
description: Irish cream and whiskey dropped into stout. Drink it fast — the cream curdles within seconds, and the name is genuinely unwelcome in Ireland.
funFact: The name references the Troubles and is considered offensive across Ireland; many bars now list it as an Irish Slammer, and asking for it by the original name in Dublin will not go well.

steps: Pour the stout into a pint glass and let the head settle.
Layer the Irish cream and whiskey in a shot glass.
Drop the shot into the stout.
Drink immediately — the cream curdles in about ten seconds.

name: Boilermaker's Daughter
description: A half of bitter with a shot of whisky poured in rather than beside — the gentler British reading of the boilermaker.
funFact: British pubs traditionally poured the whisky into the beer rather than serving them separately, which is the opposite of the American convention and produces a noticeably different drink.

steps: Pour the ale into a half-pint glass.
Add the whisky directly to the beer.
Stir once, gently.
Drink at cellar temperature.

name: Sake Bomb
description: A cup of sake balanced on chopsticks over a beer, knocked in by pounding the table. Loud, communal and not remotely traditional.
funFact: Despite the presentation it is an American invention, not a Japanese one — sake and beer are rarely combined in Japan, and the table-pounding would be startling in Tokyo.

steps: Pour the beer into a pint glass, leaving room at the top.
Rest two chopsticks across the rim, parallel.
Balance a cup of sake on the chopsticks.
Pound the table until the sake falls in, then drink immediately.

name: Flaming Sambuca
description: Sambuca set alight with three coffee beans floating in it — one each for health, happiness and prosperity.
funFact: The three beans are called 'con la mosca' — with the fly — and the number matters: an even number is considered unlucky across much of Italy.

steps: Pour the sambuca into a heatproof glass and drop in three coffee beans.
Light the surface carefully and let it burn for a few seconds to toast the beans.
Extinguish by covering the glass — never blow on it.
Let the glass cool before touching it, then drink and chew the beans.
